items.identifiedDescription: The blade Voss kept from his Watch years. Plain steel, one hand, a brass guard gone dull and an edge he still keeps honest.
Names, times, and three pages someone tried to tear out.
Sewn into Lillian's coat lining—old teeth, no inn tag. Faint lamp oil and river fog.
items.note: The Empty Coat · in Voss's care

items.identifiedDescription: Dented tin with a sliding shutter that hides the flame until he wants it seen. The slide sticks; the oil lasts one long night.
Worn leather gone soft at the seams. A few silver, a ferry token, and his finder's writ folded small—the kind of money that disappears quickly.
items.note: Coin is counted on the purse line, not in the bag

items.identifiedDescription: A tarnished tin of hand-rolled smokes, a twist of papers and a flint-and-steel wedged in the lid. Initials scratched away with deliberate care.
items.note: Steadies the hands, ruins the lungs

items.identifiedDescription: A stamped brass house token, the kind a tavern hands over for a drink or the door. Kept as part of the case record. The reverse carries the house's mark and its street, worn but legible.
items.unidentifiedDescription: A brass tavern token, river-dull and greasy at the rim. Something is stamped on the reverse, too worn to read at a glance.
